Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial workload details

Thanks Hannah and team — appreciate the call this morning. To follow up, here are the specifics we promised:

- Workload: interactive chat + summarization for internal support agents and customer transcripts. Mixture: 70% short-turn (~40 tokens replies), 30% long-form summarization (6k tokens input, ~400–800 token outputs).
- Peak concurrency target: 1,800 concurrent sessions during business hours; 3x burst for special events (approx 5,400).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 250ms for short-turn 40-token responses; long-form summarization can tolerate up to 5s.
- Token budget & cost target: we aim to keep per-conversation cost under $0.015 for the short-turn workload.
- Data controls: VPC-only, customer-managed KMS.

Attached is a sample trace and our current batching assumptions. We need a recommendation for a Dedicated pool SKU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4) and an ops playbook for elastic bursting and fallback to hosted models.

Thanks,
Alice

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial sims + SKU recommendations

Hi all — attached are the sim results and my top-line recommendations. Summary first, details below.

Top-line SKU guidance (POC -> production):
- L4 (heterogeneous smaller GPUs) for the short-turn 40-token pathways: L4 provides the lowest cost per token at small sequence lengths when using a quantized 4-bit path. We can meet 95th < 250ms for single-turns with aggressive batching and prefix cache, but concurrent warm sockets need to be large to hit the 1,800 concurrency target.
- A100 (40GB) as a balance for mixed workloads: better memory for longer contexts, good FP16 throughput; best if you want fewer nodes and simpler software stack. Works well for hybrid pools where short-turns are plated onto A100 when L4 pool is saturated.
- H100 (80GB) for long-form summarization and very large context sessions: significantly reduces KV cache misses and avoids model-splitting for 6k+ token inputs. H100 shines for latency-sensitive long-form runs where you need to avoid chunking/streaming penalties.

Sizing heuristics we used (attached sim):
- Short-turn (40-token) perf: 1 L4 instance (8x L4 pods) handles ~220 qps at median latency with batching=16; to get 1,800 concurrent qps at 95th we estimate ~12-14 L4 instances (accounting for prefix cache misses and cold-start headroom).
- Mixed pool: 1 A100 node replaces ~3.5 L4 instances for mixed workloads; A100 sizing recommended: start with 4 A100 nodes for baseline internal usage (handles ~1,000 mixed qps) and add L4s to scale short-turns more cheaply.
- H100 sizing: 1 H100 = 2–3 A100s for long-form throughput thanks to sparsity kernels and 80GB memory for whole-context. For 200 concurrent long-form jobs, recommend 6 H100s (to hit 95th <5s with KV cache).

Operational recommendations (playbook snippets):
- Warm pools: schedule warm-up windows 30–60 minutes before known events; keep minimal always-on L4 pool to cover baseline.
- Autoscale policy: scale L4 by qps with 2-minute smoothing; scale A100/H100 by queued long-form job depth with predictive signals from traffic spikes.
- Fallback: when Dedicated pool saturated, route short-turns to Redwood Hosted L4-equivalent model with reduced token limit and degraded SLO (notify via header). For long-form, queue with progressive partial responses to keep UX acceptable.
- Cost control: enable quantization profiles for short-turn models in L4 for 4-bit execution; use FP16 on A100 and H100 for long-form unless precision issues observed.

Attachments: acme-poc-sku-matrix-v1.xlsx (sizing table), latency-throughput-simulations.pdf (graphs), sim-parameters.txt.

Notes on tradeoffs:
- Memory: H100 eliminates the need for context sharding but carries higher per-hour cost; A100 is a mid-point. L4 is memory-limited and may require more sophisticated cache/eviction logic.
- Software: H100 and A100 both support the same kernel stack; L4 sometimes needs different optimized code-paths for quantized kernels — we can handle this but it adds a small ops surface.

I'll follow up with a short-run cost model and a PRD for the canary/fallback behaviors.

-Marcus

Alice — attaching the MVP mutual action plan and a simplified SKU matrix PDF for procurement. Key asks and next steps:

- MVP pool (90-day POC):
  * 4 x A100 nodes (baseline for mixed workload + simpler ops)
  * 8 x L4 nodes (short-turn capacity and cost optimization)
  * 2 x H100 nodes (capacity for initial long-form testing and to validate full-context runs)
- Autoscale & pre-warm: define scheduled warm windows for monthly events; enable qps-based autoscaling for L4 with 2-minute granularity.
- Fallback policy: map route priorities and specify notification headers (X-RDW-Fallback: hosted) and customer-visible degradation messaging.
- Procurement: we recommend a 3-month commitment for the MVP with a renewal/expand checkpoint and an agreed set of telemetry to evaluate (latency SLOs, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate).

Attachments included: mutual-action-plan-acme.docx, acme-poc-sku-matrix-v1.xlsx, latency-throughput-simulations.pdf
